meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('future, next').

examples.trans: That is the future mayor of Sineozersk!

examples.text: Это будущий мэр Синеозерска! Ну что, родной мой, за тебя!
examples.trans: That is the future mayor of Sineozersk! Well then, my dear friend, to you!

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Polite (вы) or plural. Core Russian det meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Adds a reason or an obvious truth. Core Russian part meaning 'after all, you know' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I did tell you, you know!

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: 'взять на работу' = to give someone a job
'взять на работу' = to give someone a job

examples.text: Вот и возьмите на работу Галилея.

meanings.note: For emphasis.

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

вообще-то.gloss: actually, as a matter of fact

meanings.en: actually, as a matter of fact, for the record
meanings.note: Polite or pointed correction. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Меня вообще-то Юля зовут. Вот сахар.
examples.trans: My name is actually Yulia. Here's the sugar.

meanings.note: Pointing at something. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.
Emphasis. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: In a list or a story. Core Russian adv meaning 'next; further' in everyday speech.
In a list or a story. Core Russian adv meaning 'next; further' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А дальше? Я очень волнуюсь, я к этому не приспособлена.
examples.trans: And then what? I'm very nervous, I'm not cut out for this.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'backwater, hole' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Just to become a notary in some backwater?

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть дыра.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always backwater.

meanings.note: takes preposition на: работать на заводе

examples.text: Я всю жизнь работала на заводе.
examples.trans: I worked my whole life at the factory.

examples.text: Этот завод построили много лет назад.
examples.trans: This factory was built many years ago.

examples.text: Я всю жизнь работала на заводе. Всю жизнь!
examples.trans: I worked my whole life at the factory. My whole life!

meanings.note: To bring an activity to an end. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to finish, to conclude', paired with 'закончить'.

examples.text: Марина, давай заканчивать эту опасную акцию.
examples.trans: Marina, let's end this dangerous protest.
The craftsmen are already finishing the complex repair.

meanings.en: to start working, to come on
meanings.note: Of a machine or device. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'работать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to start working; to earn', paired with 'зарабатывать'.

Withpair зарабатывать. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'работать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to start working; to earn', paired with 'зарабатывать'.

examples.trans: He earned a lot of money.

examples.text: Не твоё дело! — Это моё дело! — Я их заработала!
examples.trans: None of your business! — It is my business! — I earned it!

meanings.note: Imperative: извини / извините. Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Agreeing, often reluctantly. Core Russian part meaning 'all right, OK' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: + dative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помогать'.

meanings.note: Прямо так = just like that. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
